text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Prime Minister Hariri said: "Netanyahu (Israeli Prime Minister) has not yet shown convincingly that he is really a man in search of peace or a man to be trusted."
-Fearing Lebanese guerrillas may have its number, the Israeli army has forbidden soldiers from taking their mobile phones into south Lebanon to be able to phone home.
-An earthquake measuring 5.7 on the Richter scale hit Lebanon. No damage or casualties were reported.
-Private schools increased tuition fees by 35 percent.
-Clothes factories might be forced to close after a government's decision cutting by 10 percent taxes on imported clothes.
-Annual revenues of Beirut port decreased by 21.7 percent in 1996.
-U.A.E nationals from al-Maktoum family bought a huge building in Beirut for $53 million to reconstruct it as a Beirut Sheraton hotel.
-Chairman of Lebanese Industrialists Association Sarraf to resign from his post to protest against the government's decision to decrease taxes on imported clothes by 10 percent.
